sum: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (US86562M2098) has its next earnings report scheduled for November 13, 2026, according to Gekko. The price-to-earnings ratio was 14.11 as of October 20, 2026. The stock was trading at EUR 21.50 at Lang & Schwarz on October 20, 2026 at 5:39 p.m. CEST.

The reporting date gives investors a firm point for testing whether the group can extend the earnings momentum recorded in its latest interim period. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group's investor-relations page lists the results for the three months ended June 30, 2026, announced on July 31, 2026, alongside its fiscal-year materials. That period remains the most recent company reporting milestone listed on the page.

The November report will also provide a fresh comparison for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The structured financial figures for that period include consolidated net income of JPY 506.05 billion and basic earnings per share of JPY 39.49, both for the three months ended June 30, 2026.

The euro quote sits well inside the 52-week Tradegate range of EUR 17.96 to EUR 39.73. At EUR 21.50, the stock is 45.89 percent below that high, while the price-to-earnings ratio of 14.11 places the valuation beside the upcoming earnings date as the key market reference.

On the New York Stock Exchange, SMFG was quoted at USD 24.23 on October 20, 2026 at 11:44 a.m. ET, against a USD 15.85 to USD 27.62 52-week range. Its market capitalization was USD 93.9 billion, and trading volume reached 471,327 shares. The Tokyo listing closed at JPY 3,148 on October 20, 2026, down from JPY 3,274.

The earnings release can clarify whether the June quarter's JPY 506.05 billion net income was supported by recurring banking income or by temporary items. It can also update the market's view of capital returns, international banking and securities operations before the next reporting cycle.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group is Japan's second-largest banking group by assets, formed in 2002 as the holding company for Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), which traces its lineage to the Sumitomo and Mitsui merchant houses. The group provides retail, corporate, and investment banking in Japan and internationally, along with leasing through SMBC Aviation Capital and Sumitomo Mitsui Finance and Leasing, securities through SMBC Nikko, consumer finance through SMBC Consumer Finance and credit cards through Sumitomo Mitsui Card, and asset management. Overseas expansion focuses on Asia, including stakes in banks in India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Philippines, plus a strategic alliance with Jefferies in U.S. investment banking. Headquartered in Tokyo, SMFG's ADSs trade on the NYSE.

Japan’s SMBC in talks to raise VPBank stake to about 20%, Reuters reports
sum: Investing.com-- Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (SMBC) is in advanced talks to increase its stake in Vietnam's VPBank (HM:VPX) to about 20%, as the Japanese lender seeks deeper access to one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing banking markets, Reuters reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the negotiations.
SMBC, the banking arm of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (TYO:8316), currently owns 15% of VPBank after paying $1.5 billion for the stake in 2023, the report said.
The two sides aim to complete the transaction this year but remain divided over valuation, with VPBank seeking a substantial premium to its share price, the report added.
SMBC has been reluctant to match the roughly 40% premium it paid in 2023 and has considered buying shares in the open market rather than through a private placement, Reuters reported.
At current prices, a 5% stake would be worth about $425 million. VPBank is also discussing a share sale to foreign investors that could raise $700 million to $900 million, the report said.
The potential increase would strengthen SMBC's access to Vietnamese consumers and businesses, including insurance and credit markets, while supporting Japanese corporate clients operating in Vietnam.

items.t: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc Stock (SMFG) Closed Down by 4.78% on Aug 19: What Investors Need To Know
sum: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc (SMFG) closed down by 4.78%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is down by 1.52%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) down 1.62%; Nu Holdings Ltd (NU) up 1.50%; Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) down 1.81%.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group experienced significant downward pressure as part of a broad sell-off sweeping across Japanese equities and global financial markets. Japanese stock indices faced sharp declines driven by foreign exchange market instability, global technology sector weakness, and escalating concerns regarding national fiscal spending and government debt levels. As a major American Depositary Receipt offering direct exposure to the Japanese banking sector, the stock was caught in this wider risk-off environment, suffering heightened intraday volatility as institutional investors recalibrated risk exposure.

A key factor contributing to the sell-off was the severe turbulence in the Japanese government bond market, where sovereign yields surged to multi-decade highs. Although the broader environment of interest rate normalization structurally supports bank net interest margins and lending spreads over time, sharp and uncoordinated yield spikes present immediate headwinds. The rapid increase in benchmark yields raised investor concern over potential mark-to-market unrealized losses on fixed-income securities, particularly given the financial group's sizeable holdings of domestic government debt.

Underlying macroeconomic uncertainty further amplified selling pressure, as market participants weighed conflicting signals between expansive fiscal policy initiatives and potential interest rate hikes by the central bank. This policy friction, paired with heavy currency volatility, triggered widespread profit-taking in mega-cap financial stocks that had previously rallied on monetary normalization expectations. Despite solid underlying financial results from previous quarters and ongoing capital management efforts including share cancellations, sector-wide sentiment was dominated by macro reallocations, resulting in a pronounced intraday decline.

GGAL or SMFG: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
sum: Investors interested in stocks from the Banks - Foreign sector have probably already heard of Grupo Financiero Galicia (GGAL) and Sumitomo Mitsui (SMFG). But which of these two stocks presents investors with the better value opportunity right now? Let's take a closer look.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The proven Zacks Rank puts an emphasis on earnings estimates and estimate revisions, while our Style Scores work to identify stocks with specific traits.

Both Grupo Financiero Galicia and Sumitomo Mitsui have a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now. The Zacks Rank favors stocks that have recently seen positive revisions to their earnings estimates, so investors should rest assured that both of these companies have improving earnings outlooks. But this is only part of the picture for value investors.
Value investors also tend to look at a number of traditional, tried-and-true figures to help them find stocks that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

Our Value category highlights undervalued companies by looking at a variety of key metrics, including the popular P/E ratio, as well as the P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that have been used by value investors for years.

GGAL currently has a forward P/E ratio of 13.12, while SMFG has a forward P/E of 13.42. We also note that GGAL has a PEG ratio of 0.27. This popular figure is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also considers a company's expected EPS growth rate. SMFG currently has a PEG ratio of 0.96.

Another notable valuation metric for GGAL is its P/B ratio of 1.31. Investors use the P/B ratio to look at a stock's market value versus its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, SMFG has a P/B of 1.32.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group has experienced a notable upward trajectory as market participants react to a confluence of favorable macroeconomic shifts and strengthening internal fundamentals. The primary driver behind this momentum is the evolving monetary policy landscape in Japan. As the Bank of Japan continues its transition away from decades of ultra-loose monetary policy, the outlook for net interest margins among major Japanese lenders has significantly improved. This policy normalization allows for more robust domestic lending spreads, directly enhancing the core profitability of the group’s banking operations.

Beyond the macro policy shift, the company’s recent strategic emphasis on capital efficiency has resonated deeply with institutional investors. The group has been proactive in its approach to shareholder returns, signaling expanded share buyback programs and more aggressive dividend targets. This alignment with the ongoing governance reforms in the Japanese market, which encourage companies to trade above their book value, has repositioned the stock as a key beneficiary of the structural re-rating currently sweeping through the Japanese financial sector.

The volatility observed during the session suggests a high level of institutional repositioning. Global fund managers appear to be rotating capital into undervalued financial assets that offer a hedge against global inflationary pressures and rising interest rates. As a major global systemic bank, the company serves as a primary vehicle for international exposure to the Japanese reflation story. This influx of capital is further supported by a diversified business model, which includes strong performance in overseas corporate banking and specialized lending divisions, providing a buffer against localized economic fluctuations.
Furthermore, movements in the foreign exchange market have played a supporting role for the dollar-denominated American Depositary Receipts.

Canal Road Group Secures Equity Commitment from SMBC to Support the CRG Direct Lending Strategy
sum: MIAMI, July 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Canal Road Group ("CRG") today announced an expansion of its strategic relationship with SMBC as the bank makes an equity commitment to CRG's direct lending strategy that will unlock up to $225 million in additional investable capital. The commitment will increase CRG's investment capacity to $2.3 billion, inclusive of financing, for its direct lending strategy. In connection with making the commitment, SMBC is also taking a passive minority stake in CRG.

The capital commitment enhances a relationship that already includes a $350 million asset-based lending facility, expandable to $500 million, which CRG utilizes as a financing facility for its private credit portfolio. In addition, the two firms expect to benefit from the breadth of their combined borrower and sponsor relationships, creating new opportunities across both platforms.

Since launching its private credit platform less than two years ago, CRG has deployed nearly $1.2 billion of commitments to corporate credit borrowers in the private market. SMBC's commitment reflects an investment in the strength of the CRG platform, its team, and its prospects for continued growth. The team, led by Mike Damaso and Don Young, previously grew CBAM Partners to more than $15 billion in assets under management in less than six years before selling the business to Carlyle in 2022.

CRG commented: "SMBC has had the opportunity to observe our firm's progress firsthand since we established our relationship in the fourth quarter of 2024. This commitment to our strategy demonstrates confidence in CRG's sourcing and underwriting capabilities, the quality of our existing portfolio, and our ability to achieve the goals we have established for both the business and our limited partners. We value the relationship we have built with SMBC and appreciate the trust they have placed in our firm."

Canal Road Group ("CRG") is an alternative asset management firm that provides tailored financing solutions to companies. The firm seeks to generate consistent, attractive risk-adjusted returns through a diversified portfolio focused primarily on senior secured investments.
